title: Shared-log action ownership: FOREIGN is skipped, UNKNOWN is refused
note: The whole design rests on one hash-chained log that several reducers project. Two behaviours were in tension and both are right: an event a reducer does not understand must not be silently skipped, and an event belonging to another subsystem must not stop the log being shared. The registry tells those two cases apart. AC1 collapses the distinction toward silence, which is the dangerous direction: an authority-relevant event from a newer schema is dropped and the reconstructed state is confidently wrong. AC2 collapses it the other way, which is the failure that was actually observed -- the authority store refused a log containing 'policy.publish' and no two subsystems could coexist.

mutations.name: AC1_unknown_actions_treated_as_foreign
mutations.rationale: an event from a newer schema is skipped in silence, and the state older readers reconstruct is confidently wrong

mutations.name: AC2_foreign_actions_treated_as_unknown
mutations.rationale: no two subsystems can share one log, which is the premise the whole package rests on

mutations.name: AC3_require_known_never_raises
mutations.find: if kind is UNKNOWN or kind == UNKNOWN:
mutations.rationale: an unrecognised action reaches each reducer's own else-branch, where the message no longer says what went wrong

mutations.name: AC4_store_skips_unknown_actions
mutations.rationale: the authority store projects a log with a hole in it and reports success

mutations.name: AC5_governed_projection_skips_unknown_actions
mutations.rationale: the task projection silently drops an event it does not understand, so a task's recovered state omits whatever it recorded

mutations.name: AC6_reconstruction_treats_unknown_as_foreign
mutations.rationale: the independent reconstruction stops reporting that it could not interpret part of the log
